paragraphs: Cheshire East covers towns such as Crewe, Macclesfield, Congleton, Nantwich and Wilmslow, and children in care here are looked after by Cheshire East Council's own fostering service and by the independent agencies listed on this page. When the council made an appeal during Foster Care Fortnight in May 2022 it said more than 500 children and young people were in its care, and that the need was not only for babies and young children but for older children and teenagers, brothers and sisters who need to stay together, and children with additional needs.

In March 2026 the council began a campaign for short break foster carers: people who look after a disabled child, or a child with additional needs, for a few days at a time on a regular schedule through the year, with the same child coming back to the same carer each time. It said it was urgently looking for more, that experience of caring for complex needs such as neurodiversity or physical disability helps, and that it pays these carers £589 a week plus the age-related allowance for the child. Short break carers get a supervising social worker, peer support groups, training, leisure passes and discounts.

The council also says it does not have enough carers for unaccompanied asylum-seeking children: young people under 18 who arrive in the UK alone. Carers for these young people need a spare room and receive a weekly allowance based on age plus a fee, a fostering social worker, out-of-hours support and mentoring from an experienced carer.

If you live in Cheshire East, talk to the council and to two or three of the agencies on this page, and ask each which children they most need homes for locally, what training and out-of-hours support they give, and what they pay for the type of fostering you have in mind.
